title: policy-registry
description: Phase 4 (plan_26072506 S4.6) SHAPE contract for .claude/policies/registry.yaml -- the single source of truth a duplicated rule collapses to (CLAUDE.md/workflow.md/docs.md/references.md cite a policy_id instead of restating it). Schema version 2 (review-cycle1 remediation, subagent-summary-0/1-20260725_203232): every policy is structurally canonical -- explicit `clauses` (stable clause_id + statement, one per distinct invariant/HITL/fail-closed/exception the policy carries) replace a single flat prose paragraph as the thing evidence binds to, and `evidence` entries are objects {path, supports:[clause_id...]} instead of bare path strings, so a claim of support is machine-checkable against a specific clause rather than merely 'this path exists'. `registry.yaml` itself is now plain JSON text (a valid YAML 1.2 subset) -- this schema, and every consumer, parses it with the stdlib `json` module only; PyYAML is not a dependency anywhere in this project. Validated here by the same small generic Draft-07-subset engine scripts/completion_gate.py already implements (validate_against_schema) -- there is no second, hand-duplicated copy of these constraints. Cross-field/regex-shaped rules this validator's keyword subset cannot express (policy_id/clause_id pattern; exactly one of origin_failure/universal_invariant; remove_when substantive content; ISO-8601 date shape and ordering; next_review_due == last_reviewed_at + 90 days; explicit --as-of driven due/overdue/90-day-unreproduced evaluation; retired requires retirement_reason or a non-dangling superseded_by; superseded_by has no cycle; active/candidate cannot carry retirement metadata; every clause_id is supported by at least one evidence entry, and every evidence path is tracked, exists, and its supports[] entries all resolve to real clause_ids; removal eligibility requires removal_evidence.status == contract_e2e_green with a resolving path) are Python-level checks in scripts/policy_registry.py (the shared validator/auditor CLI) and tests/harness/test_policy_registry.py, not schema keywords -- deliberately, since this validator implements only $ref/type/required/properties/additionalProperties/enum/const/minLength/minimum/minItems/items/allOf/if-then-else (no pattern, no oneOf/anyOf).

policy.description: One registry entry. Exactly one of origin_failure/universal_invariant must be present for an active or candidate entry (Python-level, see module description) -- both are declared optional here so the schema can accept either shape. `statement` is a short (one-line) human label/summary; the substantive, individually-evidenced content lives in `clauses`.

clause.description: One distinct invariant/HITL boundary/fail-closed rule/exception this policy carries. clause_id is stable (Python-level pattern: `<POLICY_ID>.C<n>`) so evidence entries and the baseline contract fixture can reference it durably even if the statement prose is later reworded.

evidence_entry.description: A truthful, tracked, repo-relative implementation/test path plus the specific clause_id(s) it actually demonstrates, plus the exact executable assertion_ids within that path that back the claim -- an evidence entry that does not name which clause it supports, whose path is unrelated to the clause it claims, or whose assertion_ids are not real identifiers found in that exact path, is not admissible (Python-level, scripts/policy_registry.py: supports[] and assertion_ids[] must both be nonempty; every supports[] entry must resolve to a real clause_id on this same policy; every assertion_ids[] entry must be an exact AST-derived unittest method/function name (.py), anchored shell function/variable/long-option name (.sh), anchored YAML mapping key (.yaml/.yml), or exact heading text (.md) found in the evidence path's own content -- never a substring match; the path itself must resolve through the exact-listed, digest-locked .claude/policies/evidence_manifest.json with no symlink at any path component).

removal_evidence.description: Optional. Only meaningful for a `retired` policy that a future cycle wants to actually delete from this file -- removal is eligible only when status == contract_e2e_green with a path that resolves (Python-level, scripts/policy_registry.py check-removal).
